section.p: Audacity includes several built-in audio effects. Apply effects by selecting a region of audio and choosing an effect from the Effect menu.

row.entry: Effect
Description
Key Parameters
Amplify
Increases or decreases the volume of the selected audio.
Amplification (dB): positive values increase volume, negative values decrease it. "Allow clipping" checkbox.
Noise Reduction
Removes consistent background noise such as hum, hiss, or fan noise. Requires a noise profile sample.
Noise reduction (dB): 6-12 dB for mild noise, 12-24 dB for heavy noise. Sensitivity and frequency smoothing controls.
Compressor
Reduces the dynamic range of audio, making quiet parts louder and loud parts quieter.
Threshold (dB), Ratio (e.g., 3:1), Attack time (secs), Release time (secs).
Equalization
Adjusts the balance of frequency components in the audio. Use to boost or cut bass, midrange, or treble.
Frequency curve with adjustable points, or preset curves (e.g., Bass Boost, Treble Boost).
Normalize
Adjusts the peak amplitude to a target level and optionally removes DC offset.
Normalize peak amplitude to (dB): typically -1.0 dB. "Remove DC offset" checkbox.
Fade In / Fade Out
Gradually increases (fade in) or decreases (fade out) the volume of the selected audio.
No parameters — applies a linear fade to the selection.
